LUK_17_12: And when he drew near to enter a village, he was met by ten lepers, and they stood afar off;
LUK_17_13: And they lifted their voices saying, O Jesus, our Master, have mercy on us.
LUK_17_14: And when he saw them he said to them, Go show yourselves to the priests; and while they were going, they were cleansed.
LUK_17_15: But one of them, when he saw that he was cleansed, turned back, and with a loud voice praised God.
LUK_17_16: And he fell on his face at the feet of Jesus, thanking him; and this one was a Samaritan.
LUK_17_17: Jesus answering said, Were there not ten who were cleansed? Where are the nine?
LUK_17_18: Why did they separate themselves so as not to come and give praise to God, except this man who is of a strange people?
LUK_17_19: And he said to him, Arise, go; your faith has healed you.
LUK_17_20: ¶ When some of the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come, he answered, saying to them, The kingdom of God does not come by observation.
LUK_17_21: Neither will they say, Behold, it is here! or, behold, it is there! for behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
LUK_17_22: And he said to his disciples, The time will come when you will covet to see one of the days of the Son of man, and you will not see it.
LUK_17_23: And if they should say to you, Behold, he is here! and behold, he is there! do not go.
LUK_17_24: For just as the lightning flashes from the sky, and all under the sky is lighted, such will be the day of the Son of man.
LUK_17_25: But first he must suffer a great many things, and be rejected by this generation.
LUK_17_26: Just as it happened in the days of Noah, such will it be in the days of the Son of man.
LUK_17_27: For they were eating and drinking, and marrying and giving in marriage, until the day when Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed every man.
LUK_17_28: And again, just as it happened in the days of Lot; they were eating and drinking, and buying and selling, and planting and building;
LUK_17_29: But in the day when Lot went out of Sodom, the Lord sent down a rain of fire and sulphur from heaven, and destroyed them all.
LUK_17_30: Such will it be in the day when the Son of man appears.
LUK_17_31: In that day, he who is on the roof, with his clothes in the house, will not come down to take them; and he who is in the field will not turn back.
LUK_17_33: He who desires to save his life shall lose it; and he who loses his life shall save it.
LUK_17_34: I say to you that in that very night two will be in one bed; one will be taken and the other left.
LUK_17_35: And two women will be grinding together; one will be taken and the other left.
LUK_17_36: Two will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.
LUK_17_37: They answered, saying to him, Our Lord, to what place? He said to them, Wherever the carcass is, there will the vultures gather.
LUK_18_1: HE also spoke to them a parable, that they should pray always and not get weary.
LUK_18_2: There was a judge in a city, who neither feared God nor regarded men.
LUK_18_3: And there was a widow in that city who used to come to him, saying, Avenge me of my accuser.
LUK_18_4: And he would not for a long time; but afterwards he said within himself, Though I am not afraid of God and have no regard for men;
LUK_18_5: Yet because this widow troubles me, I will avenge her, so that she may not keep coming and annoying me.
LUK_18_6: Then our Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge said.
LUK_18_7: Would not God avenge his chosen ones much more, who call upon him day and night and he has patience with them?
LUK_18_8: I say to you, he will avenge them promptly. But when the Son of man comes, will he find faith on the earth?
LUK_18_9: ¶ And he spoke this parable against the men who relied upon themselves, that they were righteous, and despised every other man:
LUK_18_10: Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee, and the other a tax collector.
LUK_18_11: And the Pharisee stood by himself, and prayed thus: O God, I thank thee, that I am not like the rest of men, extortioners, grafters, adulterers, and not like this tax collector.
LUK_18_12: But I fast twice a week, and I give tithes on everything I earn.
LUK_18_13: But the tax collector stood afar off, and he would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but smote his breast, saying, O God, be merciful to me a sinner.
LUK_18_14: I say to you that this man went down to his house more righteous than the Pharisee. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled; and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted.
LUK_18_15: ¶ They brought to him also little children, that he might touch them; and his disciples saw them and rebuked them.
LUK_18_16: But Jesus called them, and said to them, Permit the children to come to me, and do not stop them; for the kingdom of heaven is for those who are like these.
LUK_18_17: Truly I say to you, He who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter into it.
LUK_18_18: And one of the leaders asked him, saying, O good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit life everlasting?
LUK_18_19: Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? There is no one good but one, that is God.
LUK_18_20: You know the commandments: You shall not kill; You shall not commit adultery; You shall not steal; You shall not bear false witness; Honor your father and your mother.
LUK_18_21: He said to him, All these I have obeyed from my boyhood.
LUK_18_22: When Jesus heard it, he said to him, You lack one thing; go, sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have a treasure in heaven; and come and follow me.
LUK_18_23: But when he heard these things, he felt sad, because he was very rich.
LUK_18_24: And when Jesus saw that he felt sad, he said, How difficult it is for those who have wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!
LUK_18_25: It is easier for a rope to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
LUK_18_26: Those who heard it said to him, Who then can be saved?
LUK_18_27: But Jesus said, Things impossible to men are possible to God.
LUK_18_28: Simon Peter said to him, Behold, we have left everything and followed you.
LUK_18_29: Jesus said to him, Truly I say to you that there is no man who leaves houses or parents or brothers or wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
LUK_18_30: Who will not receive many times more at this time and in the world to come life everlasting.
LUK_18_31: ¶ Then Jesus took the twelve and said to them, Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all things written by the prophets concerning the Son of man will be fulfilled.
LUK_18_32: For he will be delivered to the Gentiles, and they will mock him and spit in his face.
LUK_18_33: And they will scourge him and curse him and kill him; and on the third day he will rise again.
LUK_18_34: But they understood not one of these things; and this saying was hidden from them, and they did not know these things which were spoken to them.
LUK_18_35: ¶ And when he drew near Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside and begging.
LUK_18_36: And he heard the voice of the people passing, and asked, Who is this?
LUK_18_37: They said to him, Jesus the Nazarene is passing.
LUK_18_38: And he cried, saying, O Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me!
LUK_18_39: And those who were going before Jesus rebuked him, telling him to keep quiet; but be cried the more, O son of David, have mercy on me!
LUK_18_40: So Jesus stood still, and commanded them to call him to him; and as he came near he asked him,
LUK_18_41: Saying, What do you wish me to do for you? He answered, My Lord, that I may see.
LUK_18_42: And Jesus said to him, See; your faith has healed you.
LUK_18_43: And he saw immediately, and followed him praising God; and all the people who saw it gave praise to God.
LUK_19_1: AND when Jesus entered and passed through Jericho
LUK_19_2: There was a man named Zaccai, who was rich and chief of the tax collectors.
LUK_19_3: And he wanted to see who Jesus was; but he could not because of the crowd, for Zaccai was small in stature.
LUK_19_4: So he ran ahead of Jesus, and climbed up into a leafless fig tree, that he might see him, because he was to pass that way.
LUK_19_5: When Jesus came to that place, he saw him and said to him, Make haste, come down, O Zaccai, for today I must stay at your house.
LUK_19_6: And he hastened and came down, and welcomed him with joy.
LUK_19_7: Now when they all saw it, they murmured, saying, He has entered to stay in the house of a sinner.
LUK_19_8: But Zaccai rose up and said to Jesus, Behold, my Lord, half of my wealth I will give to the poor; and I will pay fourfold to every man from whom I have extorted.
LUK_19_9: Jesus said to him, Today life has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
LUK_19_10: For the Son of man came to seek and save that which was lost.
LUK_19_11: ¶ While they were listening to these things, he continued by speaking a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they were expecting that the kingdom of God would appear at that very hour;
LUK_19_12: And he said, A great man of a noble family went to a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.
LUK_19_13: And he called his ten servants, and gave them ten pounds, and said to them, Transact business until I come back.
LUK_19_14: But the people of his city hated him, and sent messengers after him, saying, We do not want him to rule over us.
LUK_19_15: And when he received the kingdom and returned, he commanded to call his servants to whom he had given the money, that he might know what each one of them had gained in business.
LUK_19_16: The first one came and said, My lord, your pound has gained ten pounds.
LUK_19_17: He said to him, O good servant! Because you are found faithful in a little, you will have charge over ten talents. [The Aramaic word Kakra, talent, is similar to the word, Karkha, province or city, as in some other versions. A talent was the largest coin, equal to many pounds.]
LUK_19_18: And the second came and said, My lord, your pound has gained five pounds.
LUK_19_19: He said to this one, You also will have charge over five talents.
LUK_19_20: But another one came and said, My lord, here is your pound which was with me, which I kept laid up in a purse.
LUK_19_21: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man; you pick up what you have not laid down, and you reap what you have not sown.
LUK_19_22: He said to him, I will judge you from your own mouth, O wicked servant. You knew me that I am a harsh man, and pick up what I have not laid down, and reap what I have not sowed.
LUK_19_23: Why then did you not give my money to the exchange, so that when I came I could demand it with its interest?
LUK_19_24: And he said to those who stood in his presence, Take away the pound from him and give it to him who has ten pounds.
LUK_19_25: They said to him, Our lord, he has already with him ten pounds.
LUK_19_26: He said to them, I say to you: To everyone who has shall be given; and from him who has not, even that which he has will be taken away from him.
LUK_19_27: But those my enemies, who were not willing that I should rule over them bring here, and kill them before me.
LUK_19_28: ¶ And when Jesus had said these things, he went forward to go to Jerusalem.
LUK_19_29: And when he arrived at Bethphage and Bethany, on the side of the mountain which is called the Place of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
LUK_19_30: Saying to them, Go to the village which is in front of us; and when you enter it you will find a colt tied, on which no man has ever ridden; untie it and bring it.
LUK_19_31: And if any man should ask you, Why do you untie it? tell him this: Our Lord needs it.
LUK_19_32: And those who were sent went away and found just as he had told them.
LUK_19_33: And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, Why do you untie the colt?
LUK_19_34: And they said to them, Our Lord needs it.
LUK_19_35: And they brought it to Jesus; and they put their garments on the colt, and they set Jesus on it.
LUK_19_36: And as he went along, they spread their garments on the road.
LUK_19_37: And when he came near to the descent of the mount of the Place of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice, praising God with a loud voice for all the miracles which they had seen,
LUK_19_38: Saying, Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.
LUK_19_39: But some of the Pharisees who were in the multitude said to him, Teacher, rebuke your disciples.
LUK_19_40: He said to them, I say to you that if these should keep silent, the stones would cry out.
LUK_19_41: ¶ And when he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it;
LUK_19_42: And he said, If you had only known those who came for your peace, even in this your day! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
LUK_19_43: But the days will come when your enemies will surround you, and oppress you from every place,
LUK_19_44: And will overthrow you and your children within you; and they will not leave in you a stone upon a stone, because you did not know the time when you were to be visited.
LUK_19_45: ¶ And when he entered the temple, he began to put out those who were buying and selling in it;
LUK_19_46: And he said to them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer; but you have made it a cave of bandits.
LUK_19_47: And he taught every day in the temple. But the high priests and the scribes and the elders of the people sought to get rid of him;
LUK_19_48: But they were not able to find what to do to him; for all the people gathered around him to hear him.
LUK_20_1: AND it came to pass on one of the days, while he was teaching the people and preaching in the temple, the high priests and the scribes with the elders rose up against him.
LUK_20_2: And they said to him, Tell us by what authority you do these things, and who gave you this authority?
LUK_20_3: Jesus answered, saying to them, I will also ask you a question, and you tell me;
LUK_20_4: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from men?
LUK_20_5: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we should say from heaven, he will say to us, why then did you not believe him?
LUK_20_6: And if we should say from men, all the people will stone us; for they regard John as a prophet.
LUK_20_7: So they said to him, We do not know whence it is.
LUK_20_8: Jesus said to them, Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
LUK_20_9: ¶ And he began to speak this parable to the people: A man planted a vineyard, and leased it to laborers, and went on a journey for a long time.
LUK_20_10: And at the season he sent his servant to the laborers to give him of the fruit of the vineyard; but the laborers beat him and sent him back empty.
LUK_20_11: And again he sent another of his servants; but they beat him also and treated him shamefully and sent him back empty.
LUK_20_12: And again he sent the third one; but they wounded him also and threw him outside.
LUK_20_13: Then the owner of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will see him and feel ashamed.
LUK_20_14: But when the laborers saw him, they reasoned with themselves, saying, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
LUK_20_15: So they cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. What therefore will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
LUK_20_16: He will come and destroy those laborers, and give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, This will never happen.
LUK_20_17: But he looked at them and said, What is it that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same became the cornerstone?
LUK_20_18: Whoever falls on that stone will be broken; and whomever it falls upon, it will destroy.
LUK_20_19: The high priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour; but they were afraid of the people; for they knew that he had spoken this parable against them.
LUK_20_20: ¶ So they sent spies disguised as righteous men to ensnare him by a word, and to deliver him to the judge and then to the authority of the governor.
LUK_20_21: So they asked him, saying, Teacher, we know that you speak and teach truthfully, and you do not discriminate between men, but you teach the way of God justly.
LUK_20_22: Is it lawful for us to pay head tax [This tax was levied on every male, and it is still resented in the East.] to Caesar or not?
LUK_20_23: But he understood their craftiness and said, Why do you tempt me?
LUK_20_24: Show me a penny. Whose image and inscription are on it? They said, Caesar’s.
LUK_20_25: Jesus said to them, Give therefore to Caesar that which is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s.
LUK_20_26: And they were not able to get a word from him before the people; and they were amazed at his answer, and kept silence.
LUK_20_27: ¶ Then came to him some of the men of the Sadducees, those who say there is no resurrection: and they asked him,
LUK_20_28: Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a man’s brother should die, and he has a wife without children, let his brother take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
LUK_20_29: Now there were seven brothers; the first married and died without children.
LUK_20_30: The second married his wife, and died without children.
LUK_20_31: And the third one married her again; and likewise the seven of them; and they died, leaving no children.
LUK_20_32: And at last the woman also died.
LUK_20_33: Therefore at the resurrection, to which one of them will she be a wife? For seven of them married her.
LUK_20_34: Jesus said to them, The sons of this world marry women, and women are given to men in marriage.
LUK_20_35: But those who are worthy of the other world and the resurrection from the dead, neither take women in marriage nor are women given in marriage to them.
LUK_20_36: For they cannot die again, because they are like angels; and they are sons of God, because they are sons of the resurrection.
LUK_20_37: Now concerning the resurrection of the dead, even Moses pointed it out (for he referred to it at the Bush) saying, The Lord God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
LUK_20_38: God is not the God of the dead but of the living; for all live to him.
LUK_20_39: And some of the men of the scribes answered, saying to him, Teacher, you have well said.
LUK_20_40: And they did not dare again to question him concerning anything.
LUK_20_41: And he said to them, How can the scribes say concerning the Christ that he is son of David?
LUK_20_42: And yet David said in the book of Psalms, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand,
LUK_20_43: Until I put down your enemies under your feet.
LUK_20_44: If, therefore David calls him my Lord, how then can he be his son?
LUK_20_45: ¶ And while all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
LUK_20_46: Beware of the scribes who like to walk in long robes, and love to be greeted in the streets, and take the chief seats in the synagogues and the high places at the banquets,
LUK_20_47: Those who embezzle the property of widows with the pretense that they make long prayers; they will receive a greater judgment.
LUK_21_1: JESUS then looked at the rich men who were casting their offerings into the treasury.
LUK_21_2: And he also saw a poor widow, who cast in two pennies.
LUK_21_3: And he said, Truly I say to you that this poor widow has cast in more than every man.
LUK_21_4: For all these cast into the house of the offerings of God of their abundance; but she out of her poverty has cast in everything she has earned.
LUK_21_5: ¶ While some men were talking about the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and gift offerings, Jesus said to them,
LUK_21_6: These things which you see will be destroyed; the days will come when not a stone will be left upon a stone, which will not be torn down.
LUK_21_7: And they asked him, saying, Teacher, when will these things happen? and what is the sign when these things are about to happen?
LUK_21_8: He said to them, Be careful that you may not be deceived; for many will come in my name, and say, I am the Christ; and the time is near; but do not follow them.
LUK_21_9: And when you hear of wars and revolutions, do not be afraid; for all these things must first come to pass; but the end is not yet.
LUK_21_10: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
LUK_21_11: And there will be great earthquakes in different places, and famines and plagues; and there will be alarming sights, and great signs will appear from heaven; and the winters will be severe.
LUK_21_12: But before all these things, they will lay hands on you and persecute you and deliver you to the synagogues and the prisons; and they will bring you before kings and governors for the sake of my name.
LUK_21_13: It will be to you for a testimony.
LUK_21_14: Treasure it in your hearts, and do not try to learn what to answer.
LUK_21_15: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your enemies will not be able to withstand.
LUK_21_16: You will be delivered up even by your parents and brothers, and your relatives and friends; and they will put some of you to death.
LUK_21_17: And you will be hated by every man because of my name.
LUK_21_18: And yet not a hair of your head will be lost.
LUK_21_19: By your patience you will gain your souls.
LUK_21_20: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its destruction is at hand.
LUK_21_21: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountain; and let those who are within it flee; and let those who are in the fields not enter into it.
LUK_21_22: For these are the days of vengeance, so that everything which is written must be fulfilled.
LUK_21_23: But woe to those who are with child, and to those who give suck in those days! For there will be great distress in the land, and wrath to this people.
LUK_21_24: And they will fall by the edge of the sword, and they will be taken captive to every country; and Jerusalem will be trodden under the feet of the Gentiles until the time of the Gentiles comes to an end.
LUK_21_25: ¶ And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars; and on earth distress of the nations, and confusion because of the roaring of the sea;
LUK_21_26: And upheaval that takes life out of men, because of fear of what is to come on earth; and the powers of the universe will be shaken.
LUK_21_27: Then they will see the Son of man coming in the clouds with a large army and great glory.
LUK_21_28: But when these things begin to happen, have courage and lift up your heads, because your salvation is at hand.
LUK_21_29: And he spoke to them a parable, Look at the fig tree and all the trees;
LUK_21_30: When they put forth leaves, you immediately understand by them that summer is near.
LUK_21_31: Even so you also, when you see these things happen, know that the kingdom of God is near.
LUK_21_32: Truly I say to you, This generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
LUK_21_33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
LUK_21_34: ¶ But take heed to yourselves, that your hearts may not become heavy by extravagance and drunkenness and worries of this world, and that day come suddenly upon you.
LUK_21_35: For like a downpour it will entrap all those who dwell on the face of all the earth.
LUK_21_36: Therefore keep watch always and pray, that you may be worthy to escape all these things which are to happen, and that you may stand before the Son of man.
LUK_21_37: ¶ During the day he taught in the temple; and at night he went out and lodged in the mountain which is called the Place of Olives.
LUK_21_38: And all the people came ahead of him to the temple, to hear him.
LUK_22_1: NOW the feast of unleavened bread, which is called the passover, was at hand.
LUK_22_2: And the high priests and the scribes sought how to kill him; but they were afraid of the people.
LUK_22_3: ¶ But Satan had taken possession of Judah called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve.
LUK_22_4: So he went away and spoke with the high priests and the scribes and officers of the temple about delivering him to them.
LUK_22_5: And they were glad and promised to give him money.
LUK_22_6: And he agreed with them, and sought an opportunity to deliver him to them in the absence of the people.
LUK_22_7: ¶ Then the day of unleavened bread came, on which it was the custom to kill the passover lamb.
LUK_22_8: So Jesus sent Peter and John, and said to them, Go and prepare the passover for us to eat.
LUK_22_9: They said to him, Where do you wish us to prepare?
LUK_22_10: He said to them, Behold, when you enter the city, you will meet a man carrying a waterskin; follow him. And wherever he enters,
LUK_22_11: Say to the master of the house, Our Teacher says, Where is the guest room, where I may eat the passover with my disciples?
LUK_22_12: And behold, he will show you an upper room, large and furnished; there make ready.
LUK_22_13: And they went and found it just as he had said to them; and they prepared the passover.
LUK_22_14: ¶ And when it was time, Jesus came and sat down, and the twelve apostles with him.
LUK_22_15: And he said to them, I have greatly desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer;
LUK_22_16: For I say to you that henceforth I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
LUK_22_17: And he took the cup and gave thanks and said, Take this and divide it among yourselves.
LUK_22_18: For I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.
LUK_22_19: ¶ And he took bread and gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them and said, This is my body, which is given for your sake; this do in remembrance of me.
LUK_22_20: And likewise also he took the cup, after they had eaten supper, and he said, This is the cup of the new covenant in my blood which is shed for you.
LUK_22_21: But behold, the hand of him who is to betray me is on the table.
LUK_22_22: And the Son of man will go, just as he has been destined; but woe to the man by whose hand he will be betrayed!
LUK_22_23: And they began to inquire among themselves which one of them was to do this act.
LUK_22_24: ¶ There was also a dispute among them as to who was the greatest among them.
LUK_22_25: Jesus said to them, The kings of the Gentiles are also their lords, and those who rule over them are called benefactors;
LUK_22_26: But not so with you; let him who is great among you be the least, and he who is a leader be like one who serves.
LUK_22_27: For who is greater, he who sits down or he who serves? Is it not he who sits down? But I am among you as one who serves.
LUK_22_28: You are those who have remained with me throughout my trials.
LUK_22_29: And I promise you, just as my Father has promised me, a kingdom,
LUK_22_30: That you may eat and drink at the table in my kingdom; and you will sit on seats and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
LUK_22_31: ¶ And Jesus said to Simon, Simon, behold, Satan wants to sift all of you like wheat;
LUK_22_32: But I have made supplication for you that your faith may not weaken; and even you in time will repent and strengthen your brethren.
LUK_22_33: Simon said to him, My Lord, I am ready with you, even for the prison and for death.
LUK_22_34: Jesus said to him, I say to you, Simon, the cock will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know me.
LUK_22_35: And he said to them, When I sent you out without purses and without bags and shoes, did you lack anything? They said to him, Not a thing.
LUK_22_36: He said to them, From now on he who has purses, let him take them, and the bag likewise; and he who has no sword, let him sell his robe and buy for himself a sword.
LUK_22_37: For I say to you that what is written must be fulfilled in me, He will be numbered among the wicked; for all the things concerning me will be fulfilled.
LUK_22_38: And they said to him, Our Lord, behold here are two swords. He said to them, That is enough.
LUK_22_39: ¶ And he came out and went away, as it was his custom, to the mount of the Place of Olives; and his disciples also followed him.
LUK_22_40: And when he arrived at a certain place, he said to them, Pray that you may not enter into temptation.
LUK_22_41: And he withdrew from them, about the distance of a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,
LUK_22_42: Saying, O Father, if thou wilt let this cup pass from me; but not as I will, but thy will be done.
LUK_22_43: And there appeared to him an angel from heaven, to strengthen him.
LUK_22_44: And he was in fear, and prayed earnestly; and his sweat became like drops of blood; and he fell down upon the ground.
LUK_22_45: Then he rose up from his prayer and came to his disciples and found them sleeping because of distress.
LUK_22_46: And he said to them, Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.
LUK_22_47: ¶ While he was still speaking, behold, a multitude came and he who is called Judah, one of the twelve, coming before them; and he drew near to Jesus and kissed him. For this was the sign he had given them, He whom I kiss is the one.
LUK_22_48: Jesus said to him, Judah, do you betray the Son of man with a kiss?
LUK_22_49: When those who were with him saw what happened, they said to him, Our Lord, shall we smite them with swords?
LUK_22_50: And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
LUK_22_51: But Jesus answered, saying, It is enough for the present. And he touched the ear of him who was wounded, and healed it.
LUK_22_52: And Jesus said to the high priests and the elders and the officers of the temple who had come against him, Have you come out against me to arrest me with swords and staves, as if you were against a bandit?
LUK_22_53: I was with you every day in the temple, and you did not even point your hands at me; but this is your time, and the power of darkness.
LUK_22_54: ¶ And they arrested him and brought him to the house of the high priest. And Simon followed him afar off.
LUK_22_55: And they kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard, and sat around it; and Simon also sat among them.
LUK_22_56: And a young woman saw him sitting by the fire, and she looked at him and said, This man also was with him.
LUK_22_57: But he denied, saying, Woman, I do not know him.
LUK_22_58: And after a little while, another saw him and said to him, You also are one of them. But Peter said, I am not.
LUK_22_59: And after an hour, another one argued and said, Truly, this man also was with him; for he is also a Galilean.
LUK_22_60: Peter said, Man, I do not know what you are saying. And immediately while he was still speaking, the cock crowed.
LUK_22_61: And Jesus turned and looked at Peter. And Simon remembered the word of our Lord that was said to him, Before the cock crows you will deny me three times.
LUK_22_62: And Simon went outside and wept bitterly.
LUK_22_63: ¶ And the men who held Jesus mocked him,
LUK_22_64: And they covered his head and smote him on his face, saying, Prophesy! Who has struck you?
LUK_22_65: And many other things they blasphemed and said against him.
LUK_22_66: ¶ As soon as it was daybreak, the elders and the high priests and the scribes gathered together and brought him up to their council chamber.
LUK_22_67: And they said to him, If you are the Christ, tell us. He said to them, If I tell you, you will not believe me.
LUK_22_68: And if I ask you, you will not answer me nor release me.
LUK_22_69: From henceforth the Son of man will sit at the right hand of the power of God.
LUK_22_70: And they all said, Are you then the Son of God? Jesus said to them, You say that I am.
LUK_22_71: And they said, Why then do we need witnesses? For we have heard it from his own mouth.
LUK_23_1: THEN the whole company of them rose up and brought him to Pilate;
LUK_23_2: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this man misleading our people and forbidding to pay the head tax to Caesar; and he says concerning himself that he is a King, even the Christ.
LUK_23_3: Pilate asked him, saying, Are you the King of the Jews? He said to him, That is what you say.
LUK_23_4: Then Pilate said to the high priests and the people, I cannot find any fault against this man.
LUK_23_5: But they shouted and said, He has stirred up our people, teaching throughout Judea, and beginning from Galilee even to this place.
LUK_23_6: When Pilate heard the name Galilee, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
LUK_23_7: And when he knew that he was under the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent him to Herod, because he was in Jerusalem at that time.
LUK_23_8: ¶ When Herod saw Jesus he was exceedingly glad, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things concerning him, and he hoped to see some miracle by him.
LUK_23_9: And he asked him many questions; but Jesus gave him no answer.
LUK_23_10: Then the high priests and the scribes stood and accused him bitterly.
LUK_23_11: And Herod and his soldiers insulted him and mocked him, and dressed him in a scarlet robe and sent him to Pilate.
LUK_23_12: And that day Pilate and Herod became friends with each other; for there had been a long-standing enmity between them.
LUK_23_13: ¶ Then Pilate called the high priests and the leaders of the people,
LUK_23_14: And he said to them, You brought me this man as if he were misleading your people; and behold, 1 have examined him before your own eyes, and I have found no fault in him concerning all that you accuse him.
LUK_23_15: Nor even has Herod; for I sent him to him; and behold, he has done nothing worthy of death.
LUK_23_16: I will therefore chastise him and release him.
LUK_23_17: For there was a custom to release to them one at the feast.
LUK_23_18: But all the people cried out saying, Get rid of him and release to us Bar-Abba;
LUK_23_19: (Who because of sedition and murder which had happened in the city, was cast into prison.)
LUK_23_20: Again Pilate spoke to them, desiring to release Jesus.
LUK_23_21: But they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him!
LUK_23_22: And he said to them the third time, What evil has he done? I have found nothing in him worthy of death; I will therefore chastise him and release him.
LUK_23_23: But they persisted with loud voices, and asked to crucify him. And their voices and that of the high priests prevailed.
LUK_23_24: Then Pilate commanded to have their request granted.
LUK_23_25: So he released to them the one who because of sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they asked for; and he delivered Jesus to their will.
LUK_23_26: ¶ And while they took him away, they laid hold of Simon, a Cyrenian, who was coming from a village, and they placed the end of the cross on him, to carry it with Jesus.
LUK_23_27: And many people followed him, and the women who were mourning and wailing over him.
LUK_23_28: But Jesus turned to them and said, O daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over me; but weep over yourselves and over your own children.
LUK_23_29: For behold, the days are coming in which they will say, Blessed are the barren and the wombs that never gave birth and the breasts that never gave suck.
LUK_23_30: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.
LUK_23_31: For if they do these things with the green wood, what will be done with dry wood?
LUK_23_32: ¶ And there were coming with him two others, malefactors, to be put to death.
LUK_23_33: And when they came to a place which is called The Skull, they crucified him there, and the malefactors, one on his right and one on his left.
LUK_23_34: And Jesus said, O Father, forgive them, for they know not what they are doing. And they divided his garments and cast lots over them.
LUK_23_35: The people stood looking on. And even the leaders of the synagogue mocked him, and said, He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ, the chosen one of God.
LUK_23_36: And the soldiers ridiculed him, as they came near him and offered him vinegar,
LUK_23_37: Saying to him, If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.
LUK_23_38: There was also an inscription which was written over him, in Greek and Roman and Hebrew, [Aramaic, the language of the Jews.] THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
LUK_23_39: ¶ Now one of the malefactors who were crucified with him blasphemed against him, saying, If you are the Christ, save yourself and save us also.
LUK_23_40: But the other rebuked him and said to him, Do you not fear even God, for you are also in the same judgment?
LUK_23_41: And ours is just, for we are paid as we deserve and as we have done; but he has done nothing wrong.
LUK_23_42: And he said to Jesus, Remember me, my Lord, when you come in your kingdom.
LUK_23_43: Jesus said to him, Truly I say to you, Today [Ancient text were not punctuated. The comma could come before or after today.] you will be with me in Paradise.
LUK_23_44: ¶ Now it was about the sixth hour, and darkness fell upon the whole earth, and lasted until the ninth hour.
LUK_23_45: And the sun was darkened, and the curtains at the door of the temple were torn in the center.
LUK_23_46: Then Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, O my Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit. He said this and it was finished
LUK_23_47: ¶ When the centurion saw what had happened, he praised God and said. Truly this was a righteous man.
LUK_23_48: And all the people who were gathered together to see this sight, when they saw what had happened, returned, beating their breasts.
LUK_23_49: And all the acquaintances of Jesus stood afar off, and the women who had come with him from Galilee, and they were beholding these things.
LUK_23_50: ¶ There was a man named Joseph the counselor of Ramtha, a city of Judea, a good and righteous man.
LUK_23_51: He did not agree with their wishes and their actions; and he waited for the kingdom of God.
LUK_23_52: He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
LUK_23_53: And he took it down and wrapped it in fine linen, and laid it in a hewn tomb in which no one was ever laid.
LUK_23_54: This was a Friday, and the sabbath was approaching.
LUK_23_55: ¶ The women who had come with him from Galilee were near, and they saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
LUK_23_56: And they returned and prepared spices and perfumes. And on the sabbath they rested, as it is commanded.
LUK_24_1: AND on the first day of the week, early in the morning, while it was yet dark, they came to the tomb and brought the spices which they had prepared; and there were with them other women.
LUK_24_2: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
LUK_24_3: And they entered in, but they did not find the body of Jesus.
LUK_24_4: And it came to pass as they were confused about this, behold, two men stood above them, and their garments were shining;
LUK_24_5: And they were afraid and bowed their faces to the ground; and they said to them, Why do you seek the living among the dead?
LUK_24_6: He is not here, he has risen; remember that he spoke to you while he was in Galilee,
LUK_24_7: Saying that the Son of man had to be delivered into the hands of sinful men and be crucified and rise again on the third day.
LUK_24_9: And they returned from the tomb, and told all these things to the eleven and to the rest.
LUK_24_10: They we’re Mary of Magdala, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and the rest who were with them, who told these things to the apostles.
LUK_24_11: And these words appeared in their eyes as delusions; and they did not believe them.
LUK_24_12: But Simon rose up and ran to the tomb; and he looked in and saw the linen laid by itself, and he went away wondering in himself concerning what had happened.
LUK_24_13: ¶ And behold two of them were going on that day to a village called Emmaus, about six miles from Jerusalem.
LUK_24_14: They were talking with each other concerning all these things that had happened.
LUK_24_15: And while they were speaking and asking each other, Jesus came and overtook them and walked with them.
LUK_24_16: But the sight of their eyes was blurred so that they could not recognize him.
LUK_24_17: And he said to them, What are these words that you are discussing with each other, as you walk and are sad?
LUK_24_18: One of them, named Cleopah, answered, saying to him, Are you alone a stranger from Jerusalem, that you do not know what has happened in it in these days?
LUK_24_19: He said to them, What things? They said to him, About Jesus of Nazareth, a man who was a prophet, mighty in word and deed before God and before all the people.
LUK_24_20: And the high priests and the elders delivered him up to the judgment of death, and they crucified him.
LUK_24_21: But we were hoping that he was the one to save Israel; and behold, it is three days since all these things happened.
LUK_24_22: And some of our women also amazed us, for they went early to the tomb;
LUK_24_23: And when his body was not found, they came, and said to us, We saw angels there, and they said that he is alive.
LUK_24_24: And some of our men also went to the tomb, and they found it as the women had said; but they did not see him.
LUK_24_25: Then Jesus said to them, O dull-minded and heavy-hearted, slow to believe all that the prophets have spoken;
LUK_24_26: Did not Christ have to suffer all these things in order to enter into his glory?
LUK_24_27: And he began from Moses and from all the prophets, and interpreted to them from all the scriptures concerning himself.
LUK_24_28: And they drew near to the village to which they were going; and he made them think that he was going to a far place.
LUK_24_29: But they urged him and said, Remain with us; for the day is spent and it is near dark. So he entered to stay with them.
LUK_24_30: And it came to pass, as he sat at table with them, he took bread and blessed it and broke it and gave it to them.
LUK_24_31: And immediately their eyes were opened and they recognized him; and he was taken away from them.
LUK_24_32: And they said one to another, Were not our minds dull within us when he spoke with us on the road and interpreted the scriptures to us?
LUK_24_33: ¶ And they rose up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem; and they found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
LUK_24_34: Saying, Truly our Lord has risen and has appeared to Simon.
LUK_24_35: And they also reported those things that happened on the road, and how they knew him as he broke bread.
LUK_24_36: ¶ And while they were discussing these things, Jesus stood among them, and said to them, Peace be with you; it is I; do not be afraid.
LUK_24_37: And they were confused and frightened, for they thought they saw a spirit.
LUK_24_38: Jesus said to them, Why do you tremble? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?
LUK_24_39: Look at my hands and my feet, that it is I; feel me and understand; for a spirit has no flesh and bones, as you see I have.
LUK_24_40: When he said these things, he showed them his hands and his feet.
LUK_24_41: And as they still did not believe because of their joy, and they were bewildered, he said to them, Have you anything here to eat?
LUK_24_42: They gave him a portion of a broiled fish and of a honeycomb.
LUK_24_43: And he took it and ate before their eyes.
LUK_24_44: And he said to them, These are the words which I spoke to you when I was with you, that everything must be fulfilled which is written in the law of Moses and in the prophets and in the psalms, concerning me.
LUK_24_45: Then he opened their mind to understand the scriptures.
LUK_24_46: And he said to them, Thus it is written, and it was right, that Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day;
LUK_24_47: And that repentance should be preached in his name for the forgiveness of sins among all nations; and the beginning will be from Jerusalem.
LUK_24_48: You are witnesses of these things.
LUK_24_49: And I will send upon you the promise of my Father; but remain in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.
LUK_24_50: ¶ And he took them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
LUK_24_51: And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he parted from them and went up to heaven.
LUK_24_52: And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy;
LUK_24_53: And they were always in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
JHN_1_1: THE Word was in the beginning, and that very Word was with God, and God was that Word.
JHN_1_2: The same was in the beginning with God.
JHN_1_3: Everything came to be by his hand; and without him not even one thing that was created came to be.
JHN_1_4: The life was in him, and the life is the light of men.
JHN_1_5: And the same light shines in darkness, and the darkness does not overcome it.
JHN_1_6: ¶ There was a man, sent from God, whose name was John.
JHN_1_7: He came as a witness to testify concerning the light, so that every man might believe by means of him.
JHN_1_8: He was not the light, but a witness to testify concerning the light.
JHN_1_9: He was the true light which lighted every man who came into the world.
JHN_1_10: He was in the world and the world was under his hand, and yet the world knew him not.
JHN_1_11: He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.
JHN_1_12: But those who received him, to them he gave power to become sons of God, especially to those who believed in his name,
JHN_1_13: Those who are not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but born of God.
JHN_1_14: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, a glory like that of the first-born of the Father, full of grace and truth.
JHN_1_15: ¶ John witnessed concerning him and cried and said, This is the one whom I said, He is coming after me, and yet he is ahead of me, because he was before me.
JHN_1_16: And of his fulness we have all received, grace for grace.
JHN_1_17: For the law was given by Moses; but truth and grace came into being by Jesus Christ.
JHN_1_18: No man has ever seen God; but the first-born of God, who is in the bosom of his Father, he has declared him.
JHN_1_19: ¶ This is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent to him priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, Who are you?
JHN_1_20: And he confessed and did not deny it; but he declared, I am not the Christ.
JHN_1_21: Then they asked him again, What then? Are you Elijah? And he said, I am not. Are you a prophet? And he said, No.
JHN_1_22: Then they said to him, Who are you? so that we may give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say concerning yourself?
JHN_1_23: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Straighten the highway of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said.
JHN_1_24: Those who were sent were from the Pharisees.
JHN_1_25: And they asked him, saying to him, Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ nor Elijah nor a prophet?
JHN_1_26: John answered, saying to them, I baptize with water; but among you stands one whom you do not know;
JHN_1_27: This is the one who comes after me and is ahead of me, the one even the strings of whose shoes I am not good enough to untie.
JHN_1_28: These things happened in Bethany at the Jordan crossing, where John was baptizing.
JHN_1_29: ¶ The next day John saw Jesus coming to him, and he said, Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
JHN_1_30: This is the one of whom I said, The man who comes after me is yet ahead of me, because he was before me.
JHN_1_31: And I did not know him; but that he might be made known to Israel, I came to baptize with water.
JHN_1_32: And John testified, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it rested upon him.
JHN_1_33: And yet I did not know him; but he who sent me to baptize with water said to me, The one upon whom you see the Spirit descending and resting, he is the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.
JHN_1_34: And I saw and testified that this is the Son of God.
JHN_1_35: ¶ The next day John was standing with two of his disciples;
JHN_1_36: And he looked at Jesus while he walked, and said, Behold, the Lamb of God!
JHN_1_37: And when he said it, two of his disciples heard it; and they went after Jesus.
JHN_1_38: And Jesus turned around and saw them following him, and he said to them, What do you want? They said to him, Rabbi (Teacher), where do you live?
JHN_1_39: He said to them, Come, and you will see. And they came and saw where he stayed, and they remained with him that day; and it was about the tenth hour.
JHN_1_40: One of them who heard John and followed Jesus, was Andrew, the brother of Simon.
JHN_1_41: He saw his brother Simon first, and said to him, We have found the Christ. [Aramaic, Meshikha, Messiah.]
JHN_1_42: And he brought him to Jesus. And Jesus looked at him and said, You are Simon the son of Jonah; you are called Kepa (the Stone).
JHN_1_43: ¶ The next day Jesus wanted to leave for Galilee, and he found Philip, and said to him, Follow me.
JHN_1_44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Simon.
JHN_1_45: Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, We have found that Jesus, the son of Joseph, of Nazareth, is the one concerning whom Moses wrote in the law and the prophets.
JHN_1_46: Nathanael said to him, Can anything good come out of Nazareth? Philip said to him, Come and you will see.
JHN_1_47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him and he said of him, Behold, truly an Israelite, in whom there is no guile!
JHN_1_48: Nathanael said to him, Whence do you know me? Jesus said to him. Even before Philip called you, while you were under the fig tree, I saw you.
JHN_1_49: Nathanael answered, saying to him, Rabbi, you are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel.
JHN_1_50: Jesus said to him, Do you believe because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You shall see greater things than these.
JHN_1_51: He said to him, Truly, truly, I say to all of you that from now on you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending to the Son of man.
JHN_2_1: ON the third day there was a marriage feast in Cana, a city of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there.
JHN_2_2: And Jesus and his disciples were also invited to the marriage feast.
JHN_2_3: And when the wine ran low, his mother said to Jesus, They have no wine.
JHN_2_4: Jesus said to her, What is it to me and to you, woman? My turn has not yet come.
JHN_2_5: His mother said to the helpers, Whatever he tells you, do it.
JHN_2_6: And there were Six stone jars placed there for the purification of the Jews, which could hold several gallons each.
JHN_2_7: Jesus said to them, Fill the jars with water; and they filled them up to the brim.
JHN_2_8: Then he said to them, Draw out now and bring it to the chief guest [Master of ceremonies.] of the feast. And they brought it.
JHN_2_9: And when the chief guest tasted the water that had become wine, he did not know whence it had come; but the helpers knew, who had drawn the water. Then the chief guest called the bridegroom
JHN_2_10: And said to him, Every man at the first brings the best wine; and when they have drunk, then that which is weak; but you have kept the best wine until now.
JHN_2_11: This is the first miracle which Jesus performed in Cana of Galilee, and thus he showed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
JHN_2_12: ¶ After this he went down to Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples; and they remained there a few days.
JHN_2_13: And the Jewish passover was nearing; so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN_2_14: And he found in the temple those who were buying oxen and sheep and doves, and the money changers sitting.
JHN_2_15: And he made a whip of cord, and drove them all out of the temple, even the sheep and the oxen and the money changers; and he threw out their exchange money and upset their trays;
JHN_2_16: And to those who sold doves he said, Take these away from here; do not make my Father’s house a house of trading.
JHN_2_17: And his disciples remembered that it is written, The zeal for thy house has given me courage.
JHN_2_18: The Jews answered, saying to him, What sign do you show us, that you are doing these things?
JHN_2_19: Jesus answered, saying to them, Tear down this temple and in three days I will raise it up.
JHN_2_20: The Jews said to him, It took forty-six years to build this temple, and will you raise it up in three days?
JHN_2_21: But he spoke concerning the temple of his body.
JHN_2_22: When he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this; and they believed the scriptures and the word which Jesus had said.
JHN_2_23: ¶ Now when Jesus was in Jerusalem at the passover, during the feast, a great many believed in him, because they saw the miracles which he did.
JHN_2_24: But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he understood every man.
JHN_2_25: And he needed no man to testify to him concerning any man; for he knew well what was in man.
JHN_3_1: THERE was at that place a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews;
JHN_3_2: He came at night to Jesus and said to him, Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher sent from God; for no man can do these miracles that you are doing unless God is with him.
JHN_3_3: Jesus answered, saying to him, Truly, truly, I say to you, If a man is not born again, [Born again in Northern Aramaic means to change one’s thoughts and habits. Nicodemus spoke Southern Aramaic and hence did not understand Jesus.] he cannot see the kingdom of God.
JHN_3_4: Nicodemus said to him, How can an old man be born again? Can he enter again a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?
JHN_3_5: Jesus answered, saying to him, Truly, truly, I say to you, If a man is not born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
JHN_3_6: What is born of flesh is flesh; and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
JHN_3_7: Do not be surprised because I have told you that you all must be born again.
JHN_3_8: The wind blows where it pleases, and you hear its sound; but you do not know whence it comes and whither it goes; such is every man who is born of the Spirit.
JHN_3_9: Nicodemus answered, saying to him, How can these things be?
JHN_3_10: Jesus answered, You are a teacher of Israel, and yet you do not understand these things?
JHN_3_11: Truly, truly, I say to you, We speak only what we know, and we testify only to what we have seen; and yet you do not accept our testimony.
JHN_3_12: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how then will you believe me if I tell you about heavenly things?
JHN_3_13: No man has ascended to heaven except him who came down from heaven, even the Son of man who is in heaven.
JHN_3_14: Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of man is ready to be lifted up;
JHN_3_15: So that every man who believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
JHN_3_16: ¶ For God so loved the world that he even gave his only begotten Son, so that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
JHN_3_17: For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world should be saved by him.
JHN_3_18: He who believes in him will not be condemned; and he who does not believe has already been condemned for not believing in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
JHN_3_19: And this is the judgment, that light has come into the world and yet men have loved darkness more than light, because their works were evil.
JHN_3_20: For every one who does detestable things hates the light, and he does not come to the light, because his works cannot be covered.
JHN_3_21: But he who does truthful things comes to the light, so that his works may be known, that they are done through God.
JHN_3_22: ¶ After these things, Jesus and his disciples came to the land of Judea, and he remained there with them and baptized.
JHN_3_23: ¶ John also was baptizing at the spring of Aenon near to Shalim, because there was much water there; and they came and were baptized.
JHN_3_24: For John was not yet cast into prison.
JHN_3_25: ¶ Now it happened that a dispute arose between one of John’s disciples and a Jew about the ceremony of purifying.
JHN_3_26: So they came to John and told him, Teacher, he who was with you at the Jordan crossing, concerning whom you testified, behold, he also is baptizing and a great many are coming to him.
JHN_3_27: John answered, saying to them, No man can receive anything of his own will, except it is given to him from heaven.
JHN_3_28: You yourselves bear me witness that I said, I am not the Christ, but only a messenger to go before him.
JHN_3_29: He who has a bride is the bridegroom; and the best man of the bridegroom is he who stands up and listens to him, and rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice; this my joy therefore is fulfilled.
JHN_3_30: He must become greater and I lesser.
JHN_3_31: For he who has come from above is above all; and he who is of the earth is of the earth, and he speaks of earthly things; but he who has come from heaven is above all.
JHN_3_32: And he testifies of what he has seen and heard, and yet no man accepts his testimony.
JHN_3_33: He who accepts his testimony has set his seal that God is true.
JHN_3_34: For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God did not give the Spirit by measure.
JHN_3_35: The Father loves the Son, and has placed everything under his hand.
JHN_3_36: He who believes in the Son has eternal life; and he who does not obey the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God shall remain on him.
JHN_4_1: WHEN Jesus knew that the Pharisees had heard he made many disciples and was baptizing more people than John,
JHN_4_2: Though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples;
JHN_4_3: He left Judea and came again to Galilee.
JHN_4_4: He had to go through Samaritan territory.
JHN_4_5: Then he came to a Samaritan city called Sychar, near the field which Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
JHN_4_6: Now Jacob’s well was there; and Jesus was tired by the fatigue of the journey, and sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
JHN_4_7: And there came a woman from Samaria to draw water; and Jesus said to her, Give me water to drink.
JHN_4_8: His disciples had entered into the city to buy food for themselves.
JHN_4_9: The Samaritan woman said to him, How is it? You are a Jew, and yet you ask me for a drink, who am a Samaritan woman? (For Jews have no social intercourse with Samaritans.)
JHN_4_10: Jesus answered, saying to her, If you only knew the gift of God and who is the man who said to you, Give me a drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.
JHN_4_11: The woman said to him, My lord, you have no leather bucket and no deep well; where do you get the living water?
JHN_4_12: What! are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well, and he himself drank from it, and his sons and his sheep?
JHN_4_13: Jesus answered, saying to her, Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again;
JHN_4_14: But whoever drinks of the water which I give him shall never thirst; but the same water which I give him shall become in him a well of water springing up to life everlasting·
JHN_4_15: The woman said to him, My lord, give me of this water, so that I may not thirst again and need not come and draw from here.
JHN_4_16: Jesus said to her, Go and call your husband, and come here.
JHN_4_17: She said to him, I have no husband. Jesus said to her, You said well, I have no husband;
JHN_4_18: For you have had five husbands; and the one you now have is not your husband; what you said is true.
JHN_4_19: Then the woman said to him, My lord, I see that you are a prophet.
JHN_4_20: Our forefathers worshipped on this mountain; and you say the place where men must worship is in Jerusalem.
JHN_4_21: Jesus said to her, Woman, believe me, the time is coming, when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will they worship the Father.
JHN_4_22: You worship what you do not know; but we worship what we do know; for salvation is from the Jews.
JHN_4_23: But the time is coming, and it is here, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth; for the Father also desires worshippers such as these.
JHN_4_24: For God is Spirit; and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
JHN_4_25: The woman said to him, I know that the Messiah (Christ) is coming; when he is come, he will teach us everything.
JHN_4_26: Jesus said to her, I am he who is speaking to you.
JHN_4_27: ¶ While he was talking, his disciples came and were surprised that he was talking with a married woman; but no one said to him, What do you want? or, What are you talking with her?
JHN_4_28: The woman then left her water jar, and went to the city and said to the men,
JHN_4_29: Come and see a man who told me everything which I have done; What! is he the Christ?
JHN_4_30: And the men went out of the city, and came to him.
JHN_4_31: ¶ During the interval his disciples begged him, saying, Teacher, eat.
JHN_4_32: But he said to them, I have food to eat of which you do not know.
JHN_4_33: The disciples said among themselves, What! did any man bring him something to eat?
JHN_4_34: Jesus said to them, My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work.
JHN_4_35: Do you not say that after four months comes the harvest? Behold, I say to you, Lift up your eyes and look at the fields which have turned white and have long been ready for the harvest.
JHN_4_36: And he who reaps receives wages and gathers fruits to life everlasting, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
JHN_4_37: For in this case the saying is true, One sows and another reaps.
JHN_4_38: I sent you to reap that for which you did not labor; for others labored, and you have entered into their labor.
JHN_4_39: ¶ A great many Samaritans of that city believed in him because of the word of that woman, who testified, He told me everything which I have done.
JHN_4_40: So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them; and he stayed with them two days.
JHN_4_41: And a great many believed in him because of his word;
JHN_4_42: And they were saying to the woman, Henceforth it is not because of your word that we believe in him; for we ourselves have heard and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.
JHN_4_43: ¶ Two days later, Jesus departed thence and went to Galilee.
JHN_4_44: For Jesus himself testified that a prophet is not honored in his own city.
JHN_4_45: When he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, for they had seen all the wonders he did at Jerusalem during the feast; for they also had come to the feast.
JHN_4_46: Then Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water wine. And there was at Capernaum a servant of a king, whose son was sick.
JHN_4_47: This man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee; so he went to him and asked him to come down and heal his son; for he was near death.
JHN_4_48: Jesus said to him. Unless you see miracles and wonders, you will not believe.
JHN_4_49: The king’s servant said to him, My Lord, come down before the boy is dead.
JHN_4_50: Jesus said to him, Go, your son is healed. And the man believed the word that Jesus said to him and went away.
JHN_4_51: And as he was going down, his servants met him and brought him good news, saying, Your son is healed.
JHN_4_52: And he asked them, At what time was he healed? They said to him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
JHN_4_53: And his father knew that it was at that very hour when Jesus told him, Your son is healed; so he himself believed and his whole household.
JHN_4_54: This is again the second miracle which Jesus did after he came from Judea to Galilee.
JHN_5_1: AFTER these things there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN_5_2: Now there was at Jerusalem a baptismal pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five entrances.
JHN_5_3: And at these entrances a great many sick people were lying, the blind, the lame, and the crippled; and they were waiting for the water to be stirred up;
JHN_5_4: For an angel of God went down at a certain time to the baptismal pool and stirred up the water; and whoever went in first after the stirring of the water was healed of any disease he had.
JHN_5_5: A man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
JHN_5_6: Jesus saw this man lying down, and he knew that he had been waiting for a long time; so he said to him, Do you wish to be healed?
JHN_5_7: The sick man answered, saying, Yes, my Lord; but I have no man, when the water is stirred up, to put me into the baptismal pool; but while I am coming, another one goes in before me.
JHN_5_8: Jesus said to him, Rise, take up your quilt and walk.
JHN_5_9: And the man was healed immediately, and he got up and took his quilt and walked. And that day was the sabbath.
JHN_5_10: ¶ So the Jews said to him who was healed, It is the sabbath; it is not lawful for you to carry your quilt.
JHN_5_11: He answered, saying to them, He who healed me told me, Take up your quilt and walk.
JHN_5_12: And they asked him, Who is this man who said to you, Take up your quilt and walk?
JHN_5_13: But he who was healed did not know who he was; for Jesus was pressed by a large crowd which was at that place.
JHN_5_14: After a while, Jesus found him in the temple, and said to him, Behold, you are healed; do not sin again, for something worse might happen to you than at first.
JHN_5_15: And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
JHN_5_16: ¶ And for this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus and wanted to kill him, because he was doing these things on the sabbath.
JHN_5_17: ¶ But Jesus said to them, My Father works even until now, so I also work.
JHN_5_18: And for this the Jews wanted the more to kill him, not only because he was weakening the sabbath, but also because he said concerning God that he was his Father, and he was making himself equal with God.
JHN_5_19: Jesus answered, saying to them, Truly, truly, I say to you that the Son can do nothing of his own accord, except what he sees the Father doing; for the things which the Father does, the same the Son does also.
JHN_5_20: For the Father loves his Son, and he shows him everything that he does; and he will show him greater works than these, so that you may marvel.
JHN_5_21: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son gives life to those whom he will.
JHN_5_22: For the Father does not judge any man, but he has entrusted all judgment to the Son;
JHN_5_23: So that every man should honor the Son, just as he honors the Father. He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
JHN_5_24: Truly, truly, I say to you, He who hears my word and believes him who has sent me has everlasting life; and he does not come before the judgment, but he passes from death to life.
JHN_5_25: Truly, truly, I say to you, The time is coming, and it is now already here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God; and those who hear it will live.
JHN_5_26: For as the Father has life in himself, even so he has given to the Son also to have life in himself.
JHN_5_27: And he has given him authority to execute judgment also, for he is the Son of man.
JHN_5_28: Do not wonder at this; for the time is coming, when all those who are in their graves will hear his voice,
JHN_5_29: And they will come out; those who have done good works to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil works to the resurrection of judgment.
JHN_5_30: I can do nothing of myself; but as I hear I judge, and my judgment is just; for I do not seek my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
JHN_5_31: If I testify concerning myself, my testimony is not true.
JHN_5_32: ¶ It is another one who testifies concerning me; and I know that the testimony which he testifies concerning me is true.
JHN_5_33: You sent to John, and he testified concerning the truth.
JHN_5_34: But I do not receive any testimony from men; but I tell you these things so that you may be saved.
JHN_5_35: He was a lamp which burns and gives light; and you were willing to delight in his light for a while.
JHN_5_36: ¶ But I have a greater testimony than that of John; for the works which my Father has given me to finish, the same works which I do, testify concerning me, that the Father has sent me.
JHN_5_37: And the Father who sent me has testified concerning me. But you have never heard his voice nor seen his appearance.
JHN_5_38: And his word does not abide in you, because you do not believe in him whom he has sent.
JHN_5_39: ¶ Examine the scriptures; in them you trust that you have eternal life; and even they testify concerning me.
JHN_5_40: Yet you will not come to me, that you might have life everlasting.
JHN_5_41: I do not receive any praise from men.
JHN_5_42: But I know you well, that the love of God is not in you.
JHN_5_43: I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me; if another should come in his own name, you will receive him.
JHN_5_44: How can you believe, when you accept praise one from another, but the praise from God only, you do not want?
JHN_5_45: What! do you think that I will accuse you before the Father; there is one who will accuse you, even Moses, in whom you trust.
JHN_5_46: For if you had believed in Moses, you would also have believed in me; for Moses wrote concerning me.
JHN_5_47: If you do not believe his writings, how then can you believe my words?
JHN_6_1: AFTER these things, Jesus went to the port of the sea of Galilee, at Tiberias.
JHN_6_2: And a great many people followed him, because they saw the miracles which he performed on sick people.
JHN_6_3: So Jesus went up to the mountain, and he sat there with his disciples.
JHN_6_4: And the feast of the passover of the Jews was at hand.
JHN_6_5: ¶ And Jesus lifted up his eyes and saw a large crowd coming to him, and he said to Philip, Where can we buy bread that all these may eat?
JHN_6_6: He said this merely to test him; for he knew what he would do.
JHN_6_7: Philip said to him, Two hundred pennies worth of bread would not be sufficient for them, even if each one should take a little.
JHN_6_8: One of his disciples, Andrew the brother of Simon Peter, said to him,
JHN_6_9: There is a boy here who has with him five barley loaves and two fish; but what are these for all of them?
JHN_6_10: Jesus said to them, Make all the men sit down. There was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, five thousand in number.
JHN_6_11: And Jesus took the bread and blessed it, and distributed it to those who were sitting down; likewise the fish also, as much as they wanted.
JHN_6_12: When they were filled, he said to his disciples, Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, so that nothing is lost.
JHN_6_13: And they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces which were left over by those who ate from five barley loaves.
JHN_6_14: Then the men who saw the miracle which Jesus performed said, Truly this is the prophet who is to come into the world.
JHN_6_15: ¶ But Jesus knew that they were ready to come and seize him to make him a king, so he departed to the mountain alone.
JHN_6_16: And when evening came, his disciples went down to the sea
JHN_6_17: And entered into a boat, and were going to the port of Capernaum. And now it was dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
JHN_6_18: And the sea became rough, because a strong wind was blowing.
JHN_6_19: And they rowed about twenty-five or thirty furlongs, and they saw Jesus walking on [The Aramaic al means on or by. The disciples were going from Tiberias to Capernaum, both cities on the same side of the Sea of Galilee. The Church of the East believes that such miraculous appearances were by the Christ, God.] the sea; and as he drew towards their boat, they became afraid.
JHN_6_20: But Jesus said to them, It is I, do not be afraid.
JHN_6_21: So they wanted to receive him into the boat; but soon the boat reached the land to which they were going.
JHN_6_22: ¶ The next day, the multitude which stood waiting at the seaport saw no other boat there, except the boat in which the disciples had entered, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples.
JHN_6_23: But other boats had come from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten bread when Jesus blessed it.
JHN_6_24: And when the people saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they entered the boats and came to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
JHN_6_25: And when they found him at the seaport, they said to him, Teacher, when did you come here?
JHN_6_26: Jesus answered, saying to them, Truly, truly, I say to you, You seek me, not because you saw the miracles, but just because you ate bread and were filled.
JHN_6_27: Do not labor for the food which perishes, but for the food which endures to life everlasting, which the Son of man will give you; for this one God the Father has sealed.
JHN_6_28: They said to him, What shall we do to work the works of God?
JHN_6_29: Jesus answered, saying to them, This is the work of God, that you should believe in him whom he has sent.
JHN_6_30: They said to him, What miracle do you perform that we may see and believe in you? What have you performed?
JHN_6_31: Our forefathers ate manna in the wilderness; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
JHN_6_32: Jesus said to them, Truly, truly, I say to you, It was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
JHN_6_33: For the bread of God is he who has come down from heaven, who gives life to the world.
JHN_6_34: They said to him, Our Lord, give us this bread always.
JHN_6_35: Jesus said to them, I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall never hunger; and he who believes in me shall never thirst.
JHN_6_36: But I have said to you that you have seen me and yet you do not believe.
JHN_6_37: Everyone whom my Father has given me shall come to me; and he who comes to me I will not cast out.
JHN_6_38: For I came down from heaven, not merely to do my own will, but to do the will of him who sent me.
JHN_6_39: This is the will of him who sent me that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but should raise it up at the last day.
JHN_6_40: For this is the will of my Father, that whoever sees the Son and believes in him shall have life everlasting; and I will raise him up at the last day.
JHN_6_41: Now the Jews murmured against him, for he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven.
JHN_6_42: And they said, Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can he say, I have come down from heaven?
JHN_6_43: Jesus answered, saying to them, Do not murmur one with another.
JHN_6_44: No man can come to me unless the Father who sent me draw him; and I will raise him up at the last day.
JHN_6_45: For it is written in the prophet, They shall all be taught by God. Everyone therefore who hears from the Father and learns from him will come to me.
JHN_6_46: No man can see the Father except him who is from God; he can see the Father.
JHN_6_47: Truly, truly, I say to you, He who believes in me has eternal life.
JHN_6_48: I am the bread of life.
JHN_6_49: Your forefathers ate manna in the wilderness, and yet they died.
JHN_6_50: This is the bread which came down from heaven, that a man may eat of it and not die.
JHN_6_51: I am the living bread because I came down from heaven; if any man eats of this bread, he shall live forever; and the bread which I will give is my body, which I am giving for the sake of the life of the world.
JHN_6_52: The Jews argued one with another, saying, How can this man give us his body to eat?
JHN_6_53: Jesus said to them. Truly, truly I say to you, Unless you eat the body of the Son of man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves,
JHN_6_54: He who eats of my body and drinks of my blood has eternal life; and I will raise him at the last day.
JHN_6_55: For my body truly is the food, and my blood truly is the drink.
JHN_6_56: He who eats my body and drinks my blood will abide with me, and I with him.
JHN_6_57: Just as the living Father sent me, and I am living because of the Father, so whoever eats of me will also live because of me.
JHN_6_58: This is the bread which came down from heaven; it is not like that manna which your forefathers ate and died; he who eats of this bread shall live forever.
JHN_6_59: These things he said in the synagogue while he was teaching at Capernaum.
JHN_6_60: ¶ Many of his disciples who heard it said, This is a hard saying; who can listen to it?
JHN_6_61: Jesus knew in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this; so he said to them, Does this cause you to stumble?
JHN_6_62: What then if you should see the Son of man ascending to the place where he was before?
JHN_6_63: It is the spirit that gives life; the body is of no account; the words which I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
JHN_6_64: But there are some of you who do not believe. For Jesus knew for a long while who were those who did not believe, and who was to betray him.
JHN_6_65: And he said to them, For this reason I have told you that no man can come to me unless it is given to him by my Father.
JHN_6_66: ¶ Just because of this saying a great many of his disciples turned away and did not walk with him.
JHN_6_67: So Jesus said to his twelve, What! do you also want to go away?
JHN_6_68: Simon Peter answered, saying, My Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.
JHN_6_69: And we have believed and known that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
JHN_6_70: Jesus said to them, Did not I choose you, the twelve, and yet one of you is Satan? [The Aramaic satana (Satan) is derived from sta, which means to slide, to slip, or to miss the mark, and applies to one who causes these results.]
JHN_6_71: He said it concerning Judah, the son of Simon Iscariot; for he was the one of the twelve who was going to betray him.
JHN_7_1: AFTER these things Jesus travelled in Galilee; for he did not wish to travel in Judea because the Jews wanted to kill him.
JHN_7_2: Now the Jewish feast of the tabernacles was at hand.
JHN_7_3: And his brothers said to Jesus, Depart from here and go to Judea, so that your disciples may see the works that you do.
JHN_7_4: For there is no man who does anything in secret and yet wants it to become known. If you are doing these things, show yourself to the people.
JHN_7_5: For not even his own brothers believed in Jesus.
JHN_7_6: Jesus said to them, My time has not yet come; but your time is always here.
JHN_7_7: The world cannot hate you; but it hates me, because I testify against it, that its works are evil.
JHN_7_8: You go up to this feast; I am not going just now to this feast, for my time is not yet come.
JHN_7_9: He said these things, and remained in Galilee.
JHN_7_10: ¶ But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not openly, but as it were in secret.
JHN_7_11: The Jews were looking for him at the feast and said, Where is he?
JHN_7_12: And there was much murmuring among the people concerning him; for some said, He is good; and others said, No, but he just deceives the people.
JHN_7_13: But no man spoke openly about him, because of the fear of the Jews.
JHN_7_14: ¶ Now about the middle period of the feast, Jesus went up to the temple and taught.
JHN_7_15: And the Jews marvelled, saying, How does this man know how to read when he has not been instructed?
JHN_7_16: Jesus answered, saying, My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me.
JHN_7_17: He who wills to do his will can understand if my teaching is from God or if I am just speaking of my own accord.
